correctness.rationale: For a fixed finite carrier and a strict partial-order inclusion P<Q, Up(Q) is a proper subset of Up(P). For every nonempty downset D of Up(Q), its lower closure in Up(P) is a nonempty downset; intersecting with Up(Q) recovers D, making the map injective. A principal lower set generated by an upset A in Up(P)\Up(Q) is not in the image: equality would force A=B in Up(Q). Therefore |Dw+(Up(Q))|<|Dw+(Up(P))|. Linear extension and the discrete order give unique chain size n+1 and antichain size Dedekind M_n-1, respectively. Inspected exact file verify_order_refinement.py and wrote a separate independent bitset enumerator; all 1+3+19+219 labeled posets n<=4 and all 3064 ordered strict refinements passed, including sharp equality cases. This finite check corroborates but is not the unrestricted proof.
